newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Explosions reported in northern Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Explosions reported in northern Bosnia.

text.p: A series of explosions destroyed a number of houses in former Moslem villages in Serb-held northern Bosnia on Thursday, an international police spokesman said.

Andrea Angeli of the International Police Task Force (IPTF), which is charged with helping to implement the Bosnian peace process, said the blasts occurred between 1 p.m. and 7 p.m. in the area around the city of Tuzla.
There were no reports of casualties.
Four explosions destroyed six houses in the abandoned village of Mumbasic, rattling windows in a nearby village whose angry inhabitants staged a protest, threatening retaliation against the Serbs.
Angeli said the crowd later dispersed and the IPTF was carrying out an investigation.
An explosion also ripped through a house being rebuilt in the village of Stanic Rijeka.
In a third incident, five explosions were reported from the village of Kardoni, not far from the Serb-held town of Zvornik.
Angeli said there was no immediate explanation for these explosions.
The blasts come at a time of tension in northern Bosnia, with Moslems moving into their old homes in some villages now in Serb-held territory.

Bosnian Serb police, in a joint patrol of the village of Dugi Dio with the IPTF and NATO peacekeeping troops on Wednesday, found two rifles, two hand grenades and some ammunition in the house of a Moslem man.
